This post introduces a user-defined function for casting **sf** objects of class
`LINESTRING` or `POLYGON` into substrings.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| fig-cap: ""
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  dev = "ragg_png"
)
knitr::opts_knit$set(global.par = TRUE)
library(knitr)
rm(list = ls())
```

## Required **R** packages

```{r}
#| label: libs
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tidy: true
#| fig-cap: ""
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
```

## The problem

The **sf** package includes [`st_cast`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/reference/st_cast.html),
a powerful function that transforms geometries into other types of geometries
(i.e. `LINESTRING` to `POLYGON`, etc.).

```{r}
#| label: 20190505_italycast
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tidy: styler
#| fig-width: !expr 500/90
#| fig-height: !expr 500/90
#| dev-args: !expr list(bg = NA)
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Four maps of Italy comparing multipolygon, polygon, line and point representations. Separate polygons and boundary vertices become visible as the geometry is converted."
italy <- ne_countries(country = "italy", returnclass = "sf")
italy_pol <- italy %>% st_cast("POLYGON")
italy_lin <- italy_pol %>% st_cast("LINESTRING")
italy_pt <- italy_lin %>% st_cast("POINT")
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1), bg = NA)
plot(st_geometry(italy), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "MULTIPOLYGON")
plot(st_geometry(italy_pol), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "POLYGON")
plot(st_geometry(italy_lin), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "LINE")
plot(st_geometry(italy_pt), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "POINT")
```

What I missed when using `st_cast` was the possibility of breaking
`LINESTRING` objects into subsegments:

```{r}
#| label: 20190505_italycastsub
#| warning: false
#| tidy: styler
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: !expr 250/90
#| fig-height: !expr 250/90
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Outline of Italy split into short line segments, with alternating colors distinguishing adjacent segments."
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1), bg = NA)
stdh_cast_substring <- function(x, to = "MULTILINESTRING") {
  ggg <- st_geometry(x)

  if (!unique(st_geometry_type(ggg)) %in% c("POLYGON", "LINESTRING")) {
    stop("Input should be LINESTRING or POLYGON")
  }
  for (k in 1:length(st_geometry(ggg))) {
    sub <- ggg[k]
    geom <- lapply(
      1:(length(st_coordinates(sub)[, 1]) - 1),
      function(i) {
        rbind(
          as.numeric(st_coordinates(sub)[i, 1:2]),
          as.numeric(st_coordinates(sub)[i + 1, 1:2])
        )
      }
    ) %>%
      st_multilinestring() %>%
      st_sfc()

    if (k == 1) {
      endgeom <- geom
    } else {
      endgeom <- rbind(endgeom, geom)
    }
  }
  endgeom <- endgeom %>% st_sfc(crs = st_crs(x))
  if (class(x)[1] == "sf") {
    endgeom <- st_set_geometry(x, endgeom)
  }

  if (to == "LINESTRING") {
    endgeom <- endgeom %>% st_cast("LINESTRING")
  }
  return(endgeom)
}
italy_sub <- stdh_cast_substring(italy_lin, "LINESTRING")
plot(st_geometry(italy_sub), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "SUBSEGMENT")
```

## An approach

One possible solution is to create `LINESTRING` objects for each consecutive
pair of `POINT` objects across the original geometry. Let's check it:

```{r}
#| label: 20190505_testspain
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tidy: styler
#| fig-width: !expr 500/90
#| fig-height: !expr 250/90
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Two outlines of Spain comparing the original boundary with a version split into short, individually colored segments."
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
test <- ne_countries(country = "spain", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
  st_cast("LINESTRING")
plot(st_geometry(test), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "LINESTRING")

geom <- lapply(
  1:(length(st_coordinates(test)[, 1]) - 1),
  function(i) {
    rbind(
      as.numeric(st_coordinates(test)[i, 1:2]),
      as.numeric(st_coordinates(test)[i + 1, 1:2])
    )
  }
) %>%
  st_multilinestring() %>%
  st_sfc(crs = st_crs(test)) %>%
  st_cast("LINESTRING")
plot(st_geometry(geom), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), main = "AFTER FUNCTION")
```

## The function `stdh_cast_substring`

Finally, I wrapped the solution into a function and extended it a little bit:

- When the input is not a `LINESTRING` or a `POLYGON`, it returns an error and
  stops.

- The function accepts **sf** objects with several rows or `sfc` objects with
  several geometries, and returns the same class as the input. In the case of
  **sf** objects, the input `data.frame` is added.

- By default, the output is a `MULTILINESTRING` geometry. This has the benefit
  that the output has the same number of geometries as the input. This can be
  modified by setting the `to` parameter to `LINESTRING`, which only casts the
  `MULTILINESTRING` object into `LINESTRING`.

```{r}
#| label: function
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tidy: styler
#| fig-cap: ""
stdh_cast_substring <- function(x, to = "MULTILINESTRING") {
  ggg <- st_geometry(x)

  if (!unique(st_geometry_type(ggg)) %in% c("POLYGON", "LINESTRING")) {
    stop("Input should be LINESTRING or POLYGON")
  }
  for (k in 1:length(st_geometry(ggg))) {
    sub <- ggg[k]
    geom <- lapply(
      1:(length(st_coordinates(sub)[, 1]) - 1),
      function(i) {
        rbind(
          as.numeric(st_coordinates(sub)[i, 1:2]),
          as.numeric(st_coordinates(sub)[i + 1, 1:2])
        )
      }
    ) %>%
      st_multilinestring() %>%
      st_sfc()

    if (k == 1) {
      endgeom <- geom
    } else {
      endgeom <- rbind(endgeom, geom)
    }
  }
  endgeom <- endgeom %>% st_sfc(crs = st_crs(x))
  if (class(x)[1] == "sf") {
    endgeom <- st_set_geometry(x, endgeom)
  }

  if (to == "LINESTRING") {
    endgeom <- endgeom %>% st_cast("LINESTRING")
  }
  return(endgeom)
}
```
The function could be improved in terms of performance. Given that it works at
the coordinate level, high-resolution objects introduce some delay.
 
```{r}
#| label: 20190505_benchmarkfunction
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tidy: styler
#| fig-width: !expr 400/90
#| fig-height: !expr 500/90
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Map of South America with country boundaries split into short segments, illustrated with alternating colors."
test100 <- ne_countries(
  continent = "south america",
  returnclass = "sf"
) %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON")

test50 <- ne_countries(50,
  continent = "south america",
  returnclass = "sf"
) %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON")


init <- Sys.time()
t1 <- stdh_cast_substring(test100, "LINESTRING")
end <- Sys.time()
kable(end - init, format = "markdown")


init <- Sys.time()
t2 <- stdh_cast_substring(test50, "LINESTRING")
end <- Sys.time()
kable(end - init, format = "markdown")


par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(st_geometry(test50), col = NA, bg = "#C6ECFF")
plot(st_geometry(ne_countries(50, returnclass = "sf")), col = "#F6E1B9", border = "#646464", add = T)
plot(st_geometry(test50), col = "#FEFEE9", border = "#646464", add = T)
plot(st_geometry(t2), col = c("red", "yellow", "blue"), add = T, lwd = 0.5)
```
 
There is a difference in performance: `test100` has `r length(st_geometry(test100))`
polygons decomposed into `r format(length(st_geometry(t1)), nsmall=1, big.mark=",")`
substrings, while `test50` has `r length(st_geometry(test50))` polygons
decomposed into `r format(length(st_geometry(t2)), nsmall=1, big.mark=",")`
substrings. In that sense, the original `st_cast` is much faster, although this
solution may work well in most cases.
